title: Ada and the Harbor
premise: Wendell Sandoval inherited a debt-ridden vineyard and a decade of anonymous letters that once kept him from giving up on it. When Ada Reyes, the harbor-town archivist who wrote those letters under a pen name, moves in next door, their friendship deepens into love even as she uncovers evidence that the loan strangling his vineyard was forged by the bank's own director. Choosing justice over her career at the port authority, Ada exposes the fraud during the harvest festival, and Wendell, freed of the debt and finally past tense about grief, chooses her.
about_author: Ansel Ravensworth is the pen name of a former maritime clerk who spent fifteen years cataloguing letters in coastal archives before turning to fiction. They write romances set in working harbors, where debts, tides, and old correspondence decide who people become.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Soil
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Ten years after inheriting Sandoval Vineyards with crushing debt, Wendell rereads the anonymous letters that once encouraged him not to sell, then meets his new neighbor, Ada Reyes, recently arrived from the port authority. Emotional beat: weary resignation cracked by an unexpected spark of curiosity.

chapters.title: Letters Without a Signature
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Unpacking boxes, Ada panics when Wendell mentions treasuring letters signed only 'A Harbor Friend' — hers, written as a teenager after her father's vineyard failed. She says nothing. Emotional beat: guilt and longing tangled together as she decides to stay silent and stay near.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Working side by side through winter pruning, Wendell and Ada fall into easy intimacy; he confesses he loves someone from long ago who never wrote back. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by dramatic irony, each hiding half a truth.

chapters.title: The Director's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Auditing port records for work, Ada finds discrepancies suggesting bank director Corliss Vane forged the Sandoval loan terms a decade ago — the same fraud that ruined her father. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing warmth; justice becomes personal again.

chapters.title: What the Vine Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell tells Ada about the girl who wrote to him, admitting she was his first love and the reason he kept the vineyard alive. Ada nearly confesses but flees instead. Emotional beat: heartbreak delivered by honesty, silence chosen out of fear.

chapters.title: Terms of the Loan
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Vane, sensing exposure, offers Ada a promotion to bury the file; her career — the thing that saved her family — hangs in the balance. She requests one week. Emotional beat: duty pressing down like weather, love making the cost unbearable.

chapters.title: Harbor Fog
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wendell discovers Ada's old drafts among her unpacked books and realizes she is his letter-writer; hurt, he confronts her the night before the festival. Emotional beat: betrayal and revelation colliding, both admitting love at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Festival Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the harvest festival, with Vane watching and Wendell refusing to speak to her, Ada presents the forged documents publicly to the port commission. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve; she sacrifices career for truth.

chapters.title: After the Verdict
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The fraud is confirmed, the debt voided, Vane arrested; Wendell searches the thinning crowd for Ada and finds her at the harbor rail, ready to leave town in disgrace. Emotional beat: forgiveness arriving faster than pride can stop it.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. One year later, the vineyard's first free harvest ends with Wendell reading aloud the original unsigned letter, then signing his reply and handing it to Ada. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved — they choose each other, openly, in the present tense.
